availableCommands.name: create-hook

availableCommands.name: create-rule
availableCommands.description: Create Cursor rules for persistent AI guidance. Use when you want to create a rule, add coding standards, set up project conventions, configure file-specific patterns, create RULE.md files, or asks about .cursor/rules/ or AGENTS.md. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: create-skill
availableCommands.description: Create Cursor Agent Skills. Use when authoring a new skill or asking about SKILL.md structure. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: create-subagent
availableCommands.description: Create custom subagents for specialized AI tasks. Use when you want to create a new type of subagent, set up task-specific agents, configure code reviewers, debuggers, or domain-specific assistants with custom prompts. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: goal
availableCommands.description: Set a goal that Cursor will pursue to completion. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: loop
availableCommands.description: Run a prompt or skill in this session on a recurring or variable interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: migrate-to-skills
availableCommands.description: Convert 'Applied intelligently' Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/*.mdc) and slash commands (.cursor/commands/*.md) to Agent Skills format (.cursor/skills/). Use when you want to migrate rules or commands to skills, convert .mdc rules to SKILL.md format, or consolidate commands into the skills directory. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: new-repo
availableCommands.description: Create a Cursor-hosted repo for the current project and push it. Use when a project has no git remote yet and the user asks to create a repo on Cursor, push the project to Cursor, or set up a Cursor-hosted remote; installs and signs in the origin CLI when needed. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: origin
availableCommands.description: Install, sign in, update, or repair the origin CLI for repos hosted on Cursor (origin.cursor.com). Use when the CLI is missing or outdated, git push/pull fails to authenticate against origin.cursor.com, or the user asks to set up, clone, or configure Cursor-hosted repos. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: rename-chat
availableCommands.description: Rename the current chat to match its focus. Use only when the user invokes /rename-chat. Optional text after the command steers the title. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: sdk
availableCommands.description: Guide users building apps, scripts, CI pipelines, or automations on top of the Cursor SDK - TypeScript (`@cursor/sdk`) or Python (`cursor-sdk` / `cursor_sdk`). Use when the user mentions integrating, installing, or writing code against the Cursor SDK; says `Agent.create`, `Agent.prompt`, `Agent.resume`, `agent.send`, `run.stream`, `run.messages`, `CursorAgentError`, `@cursor/sdk`, `cursor-sdk`, or `cursor_sdk`; asks to run Cursor agents programmatically from a script, CI/CD pipeline, GitHub Action, backend service, or other code outside the Cursor IDE; wants to pick between local and cloud runtime, configure MCP servers for an SDK agent, or handle streaming, cancellation, or errors; or is wiring Cursor into an automation, bot, or REST `/v1/agents` migration. Use eagerly rather than answering from memory; the SDK surface evolves and this skill is the source of truth for the external packages. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: share
availableCommands.description: Save, back up, or share the current project on Cursor — creates a repo (a saved, versioned copy that isn't public) even for users who have never used git, handling all setup automatically. Use when the user asks to save, back up, publish, or share their project on Cursor, or how to not lose it. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: shell
availableCommands.description: Runs the rest of a /shell request as a literal shell command. Use only when the user explicitly invokes /shell and wants the following text executed directly in the terminal. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: split-to-prs
availableCommands.description: Split current work into small reviewable PRs. Use when the user asks to split a chat, set of changes, branch, or PR. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: statusline
availableCommands.description: Configure a custom status line in the CLI. Use when the user mentions status line, statusline, statusLine, CLI status bar, prompt footer customization, or wants to add session context above the prompt. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: update-cli-config
availableCommands.description: View and modify Cursor CLI configuration settings in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json. Use when the user wants to change CLI settings, configure permissions, switch approval mode, enable vim mode, toggle display options, configure sandbox, or manage any CLI preferences. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: adapt
availableCommands.description: Adapt designs to work across different screen sizes, devices, contexts, or platforms. Implements breakpoints, fluid layouts, and touch targets. Use when the user mentions responsive design, mobile layouts, breakpoints, viewport adaptation, or cross-device compatibility. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: animate
availableCommands.description: Review a feature and enhance it with purposeful animations, micro-interactions, and motion effects that improve usability and delight. Use when the user mentions adding animation, transitions, micro-interactions, motion design, hover effects, or making the UI feel more alive. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Run technical quality checks across accessibility, performance, theming, responsive design, and anti-patterns. Generates a scored report with P0-P3 severity ratings and actionable plan. Use when the user wants an accessibility check, performance audit, or technical quality review. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: bolder
availableCommands.description: Amplify safe or boring designs to make them more visually interesting and stimulating. Increases impact while maintaining usability. Use when the user says the design looks bland, generic, too safe, lacks personality, or wants more visual impact and character. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: clarify
availableCommands.description: Improve unclear UX copy, error messages, microcopy, labels, and instructions to make interfaces easier to understand. Use when the user mentions confusing text, unclear labels, bad error messages, hard-to-follow instructions, or wanting better UX writing. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: colorize
availableCommands.description: Add strategic color to features that are too monochromatic or lack visual interest, making interfaces more engaging and expressive. Use when the user mentions the design looking gray, dull, lacking warmth, needing more color, or wanting a more vibrant or expressive palette. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: critique
availableCommands.description: Evaluate design from a UX perspective, assessing visual hierarchy, information architecture, emotional resonance, cognitive load, and overall quality with quantitative scoring, persona-based testing, automated anti-pattern detection, and actionable feedback. Use when the user asks to review, critique, evaluate, or give feedback on a design or component. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: delight
availableCommands.description: Add moments of joy, personality, and unexpected touches that make interfaces memorable and enjoyable to use. Elevates functional to delightful. Use when the user asks to add polish, personality, animations, micro-interactions, delight, or make an interface feel fun or memorable. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: design-taste-frontend
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks for "design-taste-frontend" by name or wants a frontend held to strict measurable design rules — enforced spacing/type scales, component architecture, hardware-accelerated CSS — rather than freeform taste. For general premium frontend work prefer the impeccable suite. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: distill
availableCommands.description: Strip designs to their essence by removing unnecessary complexity. Great design is simple, powerful, and clean. Use when the user asks to simplify, declutter, reduce noise, remove elements, or make a UI cleaner and more focused. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: emil-design-eng
availableCommands.description: Use when the user names Emil Kowalski or asks for judgment calls on UI polish and micro-interactions — whether/when to animate, easing choices, component feel, the invisible details that make software feel great. Philosophy and taste guidance, not a visual style pack. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: frontend-design
availableCommands.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: general-video
availableCommands.description:
Author or edit a custom HyperFrames composition when no specialized workflow fits, or when BRIEF.md sets flow: companion. Use for longer or multi-scene pieces, brand and sizzle reels, montages, static loops, static title cards, footage remixes, and freeform builds. Use motion-graphics instead for a short unnarrated motion-first unit, including an animated title. Route fresh creation through hyperframes before using this skill.
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: gpt-taste
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks for "gpt-taste" by name or wants an Awwwards-style scroll-driven marketing page — GSAP ScrollTrigger pinning/stacking/scrubbing, gapless bento grids, wide editorial typography, AIDA structure. Not for app UIs or dashboards. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: high-end-visual-design
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks for "high-end-visual-design" by name or wants an expensive agency look applied as a fixed recipe — exact prescribed fonts, shadows, spacing, and card structures. For exploratory or project-specific design prefer the impeccable suite. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-animation
availableCommands.description: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-audio
availableCommands.description:
Use when audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition needs to be mixed: fade-in/fade-out, crossfade, track gain or volume, volume automation, ducking, a music bed that fights a voiceover (voiceover carve), effects on a track (EQ, compressor, limiter, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, chorus, phaser, bitcrush), automation envelopes drawn on a track's volume or any effect parameter, or one submix bus carrying a chain, a fader and an automation clock for several tracks at once (`<hf-audio-group>`). Don't use for sourcing or generating audio — finding BGM, SFX, or making a voiceover is `/media-use`. Don't use for clip timing or track layout, which is `/hyperframes-core`.
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-cli
availableCommands.description:
Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-core
availableCommands.description: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Also covers Tailwind projects and the STORYBOARD.md / SCRIPT.md plan formats. Read before writing composition HTML. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-creative
availableCommands.description: Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-keyframes
availableCommands.description:
Use when a HyperFrames composition needs a punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns treatment, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; also for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-registry
availableCommands.description: Install, discover, and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: hyperframes
availableCommands.description:
Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: image-to-code
availableCommands.description: Use when building a visually important page design-image-first — the user provides mockup/screenshot images to match, or wants design images generated and analyzed before implementation. Covers image generation strategy (large section-specific images, no cropping or reuse) and faithful image-to-code translation. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: impeccable
availableCommands.description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics. Use when the user asks to build web components, pages, artifacts, posters, or applications, or when any design skill requires project context. Call with 'craft' for shape-then-build, 'teach' for design context setup, or 'extract' to pull reusable components and tokens into the design system. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: industrial-brutalist-ui
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants an industrial, brutalist, or "declassified blueprint" aesthetic — data-heavy dashboards, portfolios, or editorial sites with rigid grids, extreme type-scale contrast, utilitarian color, terminal/military details. Aesthetic-specific style pack. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: layout
availableCommands.description: Improve layout, spacing, and visual rhythm. Fixes monotonous grids, inconsistent spacing, and weak visual hierarchy. Use when the user mentions layout feeling off, spacing issues, visual hierarchy, crowded UI, alignment problems, or wanting better composition. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: media-use
availableCommands.description: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: minimalist-ui
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants a minimalist or clean editorial aesthetic — warm monochrome palette, typographic contrast, flat bento grids, muted pastels, no gradients or heavy shadows. Aesthetic-specific style pack; for general premium frontend work use the impeccable suite. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: motion-graphics
availableCommands.description:
A short, design-led motion graphic where motion is the message — kinetic typography, stat count-up, chart/data-viz hit, logo sting / brand lockup, lower-third / callout / social overlay, animated map (highlight regions, connect places, zoom to a location), animated tweet / news-article / headline, webpage / UI animation (scroll, cursor, callouts), or fusing a real image's geometry into a chart. Usually under 10s (up to ~30s), no narration or live-action subject; renders to MP4 or transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / multi-scene → /general-video. Unclear → /hyperframes.
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: optimize
availableCommands.description: Diagnoses and fixes UI performance across loading speed, rendering, animations, images, and bundle size. Use when the user mentions slow, laggy, janky, performance, bundle size, load time, or wants a faster, smoother experience. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: overdrive
availableCommands.description: Pushes interfaces past conventional limits with technically ambitious implementations — shaders, spring physics, scroll-driven reveals, 60fps animations. Use when the user wants to wow, impress, go all-out, or make something that feels extraordinary. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: polish
availableCommands.description: Performs a final quality pass fixing alignment, spacing, consistency, and micro-detail issues before shipping. Use when the user mentions polish, finishing touches, pre-launch review, something looks off, or wants to go from good to great. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: quieter
availableCommands.description: Tones down visually aggressive or overstimulating designs, reducing intensity while preserving quality. Use when the user mentions too bold, too loud, overwhelming, aggressive, garish, or wants a calmer, more refined aesthetic. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: redesign-existing-projects
availableCommands.description: Use when restyling or upgrading an EXISTING site or app in place — the user says "redesign", "make this look premium", "de-AI-ify this UI" about code that already works. Any CSS framework. Not for greenfield builds (use impeccable or frontend-design for those). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: remotion-to-hyperframes
availableCommands.description: Port an existing Remotion (React) composition's source to HyperFrames HTML. Use ONLY on an explicit ask to port/convert/migrate/translate a Remotion source — one-way, Remotion-only. A passing Remotion mention, reference-only code, or "make something like my Remotion video" is a fresh build (/general-video). Unclear → /hyperframes. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: shape
availableCommands.description: Plan the UX and UI for a feature before writing code. Runs a structured discovery interview, then produces a design brief that guides implementation. Use during the planning phase to establish design direction, constraints, and strategy before any code is written. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: stitch-design-taste
availableCommands.description: Use when producing a DESIGN.md spec for Google Stitch or another agent/tool to consume — a written premium design system (typography, color, layout, motion rules) rather than UI code. Not for implementing the interface directly. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: talking-head-recut
availableCommands.description: Package an existing talking-head / interview / podcast video with timed, designed GRAPHIC OVERLAY cards — kinetic titles, lower-thirds, data callouts, quotes, side panels, picture-in-picture — synced to the transcript, on a 16:9 / 9:16 / 4:5 canvas of your choice; the clip plays untouched underneath. Trigger on "graphic overlays", "on-screen graphics", "package / dress up my video". Not plain subtitles (/embedded-captions). Unclear → /hyperframes. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: typeset
availableCommands.description: Improves typography by fixing font choices, hierarchy, sizing, weight, and readability so text feels intentional. Use when the user mentions fonts, type, readability, text hierarchy, sizing looks off, or wants more polished, intentional typography. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: ui-design
availableCommands.description: Orchestrates Brennen's frontend design skill suite for any web UI, page, landing, dashboard, component, or restyle. Use when building or changing user-visible interface, HTML/CSS/React UI, a website, or when the user mentions design, polish, layout, typography, or "make this look good". Passing Lighthouse/axe is not sufficient — generic AI aesthetics are a failure. Read and follow the linked skills; do not invent a parallel process. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: find-skills
availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-amend
availableCommands.description:
Amend a published CLI from one of two input sources: (1) dogfood mode mines the active Claude Code session transcript for friction (missing flags, hand- rolled API payloads, silent-null returns); (2) direct-input mode accepts user-supplied asks (rename a command, add commands or feeds, fix a named bug, optionally sniff the source site for new endpoints). Confirms scope with the user, plans + executes the fix autonomously, scrubs PII, and opens a PR against mvanhorn/printing-press-library. Two user-in-loop checkpoints: scope after capture, PR draft before open. Trigger phrases: "amend the CLI", "submit a patch", "fix what I just dogfooded", "open a PR for this CLI", "patch this CLI", "add features to my CLI", "rename this command", "add these feeds to <cli>", "sniff for new APIs in <cli>", "amend with these ideas", "use printing-press-amend", "run printing-press-amend".
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-catalog
availableCommands.description: DEPRECATED — do not use. Superseded by the /printing-press skill, which checks the built-in catalog automatically (or `cli-printing-press catalog list` in a terminal). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-import
availableCommands.description:
Bring a published CLI from the public library into the internal library so it's identical to a freshly-generated copy — module path reverted, manuscripts placed alongside, ready for /printing-press-polish or /printing-press-emboss. Use when the public library has a CLI you don't have locally, or to recover from a broken/lost internal copy. Trigger phrases: "import the CLI", "bring it into my library", "fetch from public library", "I don't have it locally yet".
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-polish
availableCommands.description:
Polish a generated CLI to pass verification and become publish-ready. Runs diagnostics (dogfood, verify, scorecard, go vet, gosec), automatically fixes all issues (verify failures, static-analysis findings, dead code, descriptions, README, MCP tool quality), reports the before/after delta, and offers to publish. Use after any /printing-press run, or on any CLI in $PRESS_LIBRARY/. Trigger phrases: "polish", "improve the CLI", "fix verify", "make it publish-ready", "clean up the CLI", "get this ready to ship".
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-publish
availableCommands.description: Publish a generated CLI to the printing-press-library repo (invoked by /printing-press) (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-reprint
availableCommands.description:
Regenerate an existing printed CLI from scratch under the current Printing Press, with prior research, prior novel features, and prior patches (post-publish hand-fixes) carried into the writing pipeline as reconciliation context rather than dropped on the floor. Pulls the CLI from the public library if it isn't local, recommends reuse-vs-redo of prior research based on age, then hands off to /printing-press with the right context. Use when a machine upgrade would benefit a published CLI more than manual polish. Trigger phrases: "reprint <api>", "regenerate <api>", "redo the <api> CLI", "rebuild <api> from scratch", "this CLI would benefit from a reprint".
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-retro
availableCommands.description:
Run a retrospective after generating a CLI. Identifies systemic improvements to the Printing Press — templates, Go binary, skill instructions, catalog — so the next CLI comes out better. Creates a GitHub issue with actionable findings when there are Printing Press fixes to make. Use after any /printing-press run. Trigger phrases: "retro", "retrospective", "what went wrong", "improve the press", "post-mortem", "lessons learned", "what can we improve", "file a retro", "submit findings".
 (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press-score
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to score, grade, or compare printing-press-generated CLIs (against the Steinberger bar, or two CLIs side-by-side). Also invoked internally by the /printing-press pipeline. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: printing-press
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to generate, build, or ship a CLI from an API — "build a Notion CLI", "make a CLI for <service>", "turn this API/spec/docs into a CLI" — from a vendor name, an OpenAPI/Postman spec, a docs URL, or a HAR capture; or when the user invokes printing-press by name (including codex mode and --spec/--har runs). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: remotion-best-practices
availableCommands.description: Use when writing, reviewing, or debugging any Remotion code (React-based video) — compositions, sequences, timing/interpolation, assets, or rendering issues. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: todoist-cli
availableCommands.description: Manage Todoist tasks, projects, labels, filters, sections, comments, reminders, and workspaces via the `td` CLI. Use when the user wants to view, create, update, complete, or organize Todoist items, or mentions tasks, inbox, today, upcoming, projects, labels, or filters. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: todoist-setup
availableCommands.description: Brennen's personal Todoist, run as a GTD system where Todoist projects are areas of focus and a GTD project is a parent task labeled @project holding its next actions as subtasks. Covers the capture/clarify/organize model, the areas-vs-projects split, the YouTube idea pipeline, the three-axis label taxonomy, the no-dates/no-priority policy, next-action phrasing rules, and the weekly review procedure. This skill should be used alongside the todoist-cli skill whenever working with Todoist: capturing, triaging or processing the inbox, labeling, reviewing, or picking what to work on, and whenever the user mentions Todoist, `td`, GTD, inbox, next actions, weekly review, or an area by name (Youtube, Domo, Dev, Career, Gridiron Ledger, AgentJoy, Personal). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: add-memory
availableCommands.description: Capture a project-level Syntaur memory (durable context like a convention, decision rationale, or constraint) under a project's `memories/` directory. Use when the user wants to "save this to memory", "remember for the project", "capture this decision", "add a project memory", or pin reusable context that should outlive any single assignment. Writes via the CLI so the CLI-managed `_index.md` is never touched directly. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: add-resource
availableCommands.description: Register a project-level resource (link to a dashboard, doc, ticket, or external system) under a Syntaur project. Use when the user wants to "add a resource", "save this link to the project", "track this dashboard", "add a reference doc", or otherwise capture a pointer to an external system the project depends on. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: capture-artifacts
availableCommands.description: Capture typed proof artifacts (screenshot, video, asciinema, http transcript, text note) for the active Syntaur assignment so a human reviewer can verify the work in seconds without re-running it. Use after a meaningful change is verified, especially when an acceptance criterion is now demonstrably met. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: clear-assignment
availableCommands.description: Clear the active Syntaur assignment from the current session without transitioning lifecycle state. Use when the user wants to drop, release, unclaim, abandon, or clear assignment context — e.g., "clear my assignment", "drop this assignment", "release context", "unclaim this", "I'm not actually working on this anymore". Does not mark the assignment complete or failed. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: complete-assignment
availableCommands.description: Write a handoff and transition the current Syntaur assignment to review or completed. Use when the user wants to finish an assignment, write a handoff, or submit work for review. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: create-assignment
availableCommands.description: Create a new Syntaur assignment within a project (or as a standalone one-off). Use when the user wants to add a task, create an assignment, or break down work within a Syntaur project. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: create-project
availableCommands.description: Create a new Syntaur project with full scaffolding (manifest, indexes, resources, memories). Use when the user wants to start a new project or initiative in Syntaur. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: grab-assignment
availableCommands.description: Discover and claim a pending Syntaur assignment from a project (or a standalone one-off). Use when the user wants to start working on a Syntaur assignment, claim a task, or set up their working context. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: list-assignments
availableCommands.description: List Syntaur assignments across all projects with filters by status, project, tag, and age. Use when the user wants to "see all assignments", "list pending work", "show in_progress assignments", "what's open", "find assignments tagged X", or otherwise query the cross-project board non-interactively. Different from the interactive `browse` TUI — emits scriptable output (table or JSON). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: log-progress
availableCommands.description: Append a timestamped entry to the active assignment's `progress.md`, bumping `entryCount` and `updated` in its frontmatter. Use after every meaningful action — completing an acceptance criterion, finishing a plan task, hitting a blocker, deciding on an approach — per the Keep Records Updated playbook. Triggers on "log progress", "note progress", "record this in progress", or whenever the playbook says to update records. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: manage-statuses
availableCommands.description: Manage custom assignment statuses and transitions in Syntaur. Use when the user wants to add a status, customize a workflow stage, rename a status, remove or reorder statuses, define a custom transition, change which states are terminal (the "done state"), or otherwise edit the `statuses:` block in `~/.syntaur/config.md`. Triggers on phrases like "add a status", "custom status", "rename a status", "workflow stage", "change my workflow", "terminal status", "done state". (user skill)

availableCommands.name: plan-assignment
availableCommands.description: Create a detailed implementation plan for the current Syntaur assignment. Use when the user wants to plan their work, write a plan file, or design an approach for an active assignment. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: replan
availableCommands.description: Create a new versioned plan (`plan-v<N>.md`) for the active Syntaur assignment after the current plan has been implemented (or a major scope shift makes editing the existing plan misleading). Use when the user wants to "create plan-v2", "replan", "version the plan", "make a new plan revision", or when work needs another round under the Plan Versioning playbook. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: resume-session
availableCommands.description: Re-orient a fresh Syntaur session on the active assignment without re-reading the full transcript. Loads the latest saved session summary, `.syntaur/context.json`, and any open handoff. Use when the user says "resume", "pick up where we left off", "continue this assignment", or after a compact / new session start. Symmetric counterpart to `/save-session-summary`. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: save-session-summary
availableCommands.description: Write a per-session continuity summary so a future session can resume cleanly without re-reading the full transcript. Use when the user asks to save session state, prepare to compact, or hand off mid-assignment to a new session of the same agent. Triggered by `/save-session-summary`, by Codex's PreCompact hook, or when the user says "save the session" / "before we compact" / similar. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: set-workspace
availableCommands.description: Populate the four `workspace.*` fields (repository, worktreePath, branch, parentBranch) in the active assignment's `assignment.md` frontmatter before any implementation code is written. Use after creating a worktree, picking a branch, or any time the user wants to "set the workspace", "wire the assignment to a branch", or per the Workspace Before Code playbook. Validates frontmatter via `syntaur doctor --assignment --json` before writing — refuses to touch a malformed file. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: startup-analyst
availableCommands.description: Use this skill when the user wants skeptical market research on a startup idea, including competitor analysis, open source alternatives, real user pain points, and an evidence-backed go/no-go recommendation. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: syntaur-protocol
availableCommands.description: Use when the user mentions Syntaur, projects, assignments, files under ~/.syntaur/, assignment.md, plan*.md, progress.md, comments.md, handoff.md, .syntaur/context.json, lifecycle states, or write boundaries. Core protocol knowledge for any AI agent working within Syntaur (protocol v2.0). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: syntaur-worktree
availableCommands.description: Create a git worktree for a Syntaur assignment under `<repo>/.worktrees/<branch>`, claim the assignment, and bind the new workspace to the agent session — all in one move. Use when the user wants to "make a worktree", "branch + worktree for this assignment", "spin up an isolated workspace", or set up parallel work on a different assignment. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: tax-prep-agent
availableCommands.description: Use this skill when the user wants help preparing or reviewing a U.S. individual income tax return, especially federal plus Utah, with official web verification, explicit question-asking, sub-agents, todo lists, scratchpads, and code-based calculations. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: track-server
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to register, refresh, remove, or list tracked tmux dev-server sessions for the Syntaur dashboard. Triggers on "/track-server", "track this server", "register this dev server", or similar — distinct from /track-session which registers Codex agent sessions. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: track-session
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to track, register, or log this Codex session in the Syntaur dashboard — standalone or linked to a project/assignment. Triggers on "/track-session", "track this session", "register this session in syntaur", or similar. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: video-use
availableCommands.description: Edit any video by conversation. Transcribe, cut, color grade, generate overlay animations, burn subtitles — for talking heads, montages, tutorials, travel, interviews. No presets, no menus. Ask questions, confirm the plan, execute, iterate, persist. Production-correctness rules are hard; everything else is artistic freedom. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: youtube-video-editor
availableCommands.description: Turn folders of staged screen recordings, talking-head takes, narration, B-roll, and audio into polished long-form YouTube videos. Use when the user asks to inventory footage, select the best takes, remove mistakes or dead air, synchronize screen demonstrations with speech, create a rough or final cut, add captions or branded motion graphics, revise an existing video-use edit, or produce a launch-ready YouTube export using video-use and HyperFrames. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: pp-tella
availableCommands.description: Every Tella API operation behind one CLI, with a local SQLite store, FTS5 transcript search, and webhook tooling... Trigger phrases: `search tella transcripts`, `find tella videos`, `list tella playlists`, `tail tella webhooks`, `export tella captions`, `use tella`, `run tella`. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: show-skills
availableCommands.description: Show the user's available skills, especially hidden on-demand skills that are not auto-loaded. Use when the user asks to "show my skills", "list hidden skills", "what skills do I have", "show available skills", or "show on-demand skills". (user skill)

availableCommands.name: source-command-todolist-clear
availableCommands.description: Clear all items from the active plan (keeps the plan) (user skill)

availableCommands.name: source-command-todolist-implement
availableCommands.description: Implement all items in the active plan (user skill)

availableCommands.name: source-command-todolist-list
availableCommands.description: List all plans in this project (user skill)

availableCommands.name: source-command-todolist-view
availableCommands.description: View the active plan (user skill)
